texts.preamble: Dhanasekhar. P vs Suhalya Travels Pvt Ltd on 14 October, 2025 Kabc020101592019 Before The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru. (Scch-3) Dated This The 14th Day Of October 2025 Present: Sri.B.S.HONNASWAMY (B.A., Ll.M) Vii Addl. Scj and Acjm, Member, Mact-3, Bengaluru. M.V.C. No.2200/2019 and M.V.C. No.4768/2020
texts.facts: They have spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies Dhanasekhar. ceremony of the deceased. It is contended that, Prior to the accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 24 years and was running own business as "Event Organizer and Party planner and organizing events and functions booked by his clients like Hotels, Kalyana Mantapa's and other marriage functions and birth day celebrations and he was employed 4 to 6 members for his event management work and he has also obtained house on rent for workers stay at R.T. Nagar, Seethappa Layout, Bengaluru by paying rent of Rs.7,000/- p.m, from that he has also entered into contract agreement with M/s Cherish Kadubeesanahalli for decoration contract w.e.f 01.09.2018 to 01.09.2019 by paying Rs.1,50,000/- for one year and earning sum of Rs.1,25,000/- p.m and he was only bread earner in the family and petitioners are depending upon the earnings of the deceased. If he would alive, he could have earn sum of Rs.2,00,000/- to Rs.3,00,000/- in future. Due to death of the deceased, the petitioners have lost love and affection and became destitutes, the petitioners are put to mental shock and agony and suffering from depression. (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.2200/2019 C/w M.V.C.No.4768/2020 b) Immediately after the accident the petitioner in M.V.C.No.4768/2020 was shifted to Manasa hospital, Devanahalli, for first aid, then he was shifted to St. John's hospital, Bengaluru, for better treatment, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient from 05.12.2018 to 10.12.2018 and he has undergone surgery and subsequently he is on regular treatment. It is contended that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was aged about 26 years and was working as Flower Decorator / Event Management, Bengaluru and earning Rs.40,000/- p.m. Due to accidental injuries, he is unable to ride bike or do any other day to day activities without the support of helper and has become permanent disabled. 04 . The petitioners contended that, accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending Innova Car and in this regard the BIAL Traffic Police have registered a case against driver of Dhanasekhar. P vs Suhalya Travels Pvt Ltd on 14 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133072072/ 5 the offending car in Crime No.173/2018 for the offences punishable U/Sec 279, 337, 304(A) of IPC. The respondent No.1 is the RC Owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.2200/2019 C/w M.V.C.No.4768/2020 Rs.70,00,000/- and Rs.28,00,000/- respectively to the petitioners together with costs and interest at the rate of 18% p.a. 05. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels and filed objections in both cases. Later the counsel for the petitioners have filed application Under Order 1 Rule 10(2) R/w Sec.151 of CPC to implead proposed respondents No.3 to 8, as respondent no.3 to 8 to the proceedings as they are all Charge sheeted accused. The said application was allowed by this court on 22-11-2024. Later the respondent no.3 and 5 were appeared before the tribunal through their respective counsel, but not filed written statement. The respondent no.4, 6 to 8 were not appeared before the tribunal, hence they were placed exparte. 06. The respondent No.1 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioners. While admitting about ownership of the offending vehicle Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-NB-9119 this respondent contended that he got insured said vehicle with respondent no.2. The D.L. to the driver and (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.2200/2019 C/w M.V.C.No.4768/2020 insurance policy was in force as on the date of accident, hence respondent no.2 has to indemnify the respondent no.1. Further denied age, income, occupation of deceased person in MVC.2200/2019 and Petitioner in MVC.4768/2020 and manner of accident, involvement of the vehicle, expenses incurred by the petitioner/s, dependency of the petitioners with the deceased persons. Further denied the expenses incurred by the petitioners towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies ceremony of the deceased and also denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner and expenses incurred by Dhanasekhar. P vs Suhalya Travels Pvt Ltd on 14 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133072072/ 6 him towards medication and other incidental charges in MVC.4768/2020. It is further contended that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of deceased P.Sathish and not on the part of the driver of offending vehicle. The compensation claimed by the petitioners are highly excessive, exaggerated and hence, pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.1. 07. The respondent No.2 in its written statement contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case. (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.2200/2019 C/w M.V.C.No.4768/2020 Further denied the entire case of the petitioners. While admitting about issuance of insurance policy in respect of Innova Car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-NB-9119 this respondent restricted its liability to the terms and conditions of the insurance policy. Further contended that the driver of offending vehicle did not posses valid D.L. to the said vehicle as on the date of accident, hence there is a violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy. This respondent took specific contention that the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the driver of deceased vehicle, hence the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties. Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased in MVC.2200/2019 and also petitioner in MVC.4768/2020 and also denied the expenses incurred towards funeral and obsequies ceremony of the deceased and expenses incurred towards medication and other incidental charges of the injured petitioner. Based on the aforesaid pleadings and documents available on record, this tribunal framed the following:- ISSUES IN MVC No.2200/2019 Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 04-12-2018 at about 11-50 p.m., near Kannamangala Palya gate, Devanahalli Taluk, Bangalore Rural District, due to rash and negligent act of driving of the driver of Innova car bearing registration No.KA-03-NB-9119 as alleged in the petition? (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.2200/2019 C/w M.V.C.No.4768/2020 2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom? 3. What Order or Award? 09. In order to prove their case, the Petitioner No.2 in MVC.2200/2019 got examined as PW.1 and got marked documents as Ex.P1 to 24. The petitioner in MVC.4768/2020 got examined as PW.2 and got marked documents as Ex.P25 to 34 closed their side evidence. Further got examined its State Head Legal as RW.2 and got marked documents as Ex.R1 and 2 and closed its side evidence. respondent No.1 did not adduced any evidence on his behalf. 23. The petitioner No.1 is the father, petitioner No.2 is the mother, petitioner No.3 & 4 are sisters of the deceased. Therefore the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads: Sl. Head of Amount in No. Compensation Rs. 1. Loss of Dependency (After Rs. 18,90,000-00 deducting 50% of the income towards personal and living expenses) 2. Loss of filial consortium (to Rs. 96,800-00 petitioners No.1 and 2) Dhanasekhar.P vs Suhalya Travels Pvt Ltd on 14 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133072072/ 14 3. Loss of love and affection Rs. 80,000-00 (to petitioner No.3 & 4) 4. Loss of estate Rs. 19,500-00 Total Rs. 21,05,800-00 27. Pain and sufferings:- As per Ex.P25 Wound certificate issued by Manasa Hospital, As per Ex.P.25 Wound certificate the petitioner has sustained following injuries: Fracture of left clavicle & Fracture of left 1st rib. Therefore this tribunal awarded reasonable compensation of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
texts.arguments: It is contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant, hence, prays to dismiss the petition with costs. As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 15 to 25 years is "18". 20. In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased. 22 . In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case in respect to loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years. In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram alias Churu Ram reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, the petitioner No.3 & 4 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of love and affection of their deceased brother. 25. The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 26 years and was working as Flower Decorator / Event Management, Bengaluru and earning Rs.40,000/- p.m.
